properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured on the 0.80.0, 0.83.5 and main kits with the 0.87.0 binary): a kit removed by hand comes back on `reflow2 update` because the receipt's presence is the only test of "a kit is installed here", and a missing kit file is by design read as "accept the kit copy", never as "removed"
properties.source: field log, Anthony's work machine, 2026-10-13 (0.83.5), relayed 2026-10-19
properties.statement:
SYMPTOM (field, 0.83.5): `reflow2 update` in 11 hub-member repos whose reflow2 kit had been deleted by hand recreated ~72 files (AGENTS.md, .github/{skills,prompts,hooks,instructions}) and appended lines to tracked .gitignore, .gitattributes, AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md; the one repo with no .reflow2/kit-version.json was refused ("carries a design but no installed kit … reflow2 init").

MEASURED 2026-10-19 in scratch git repos with a store, binary 0.87.0, kits extracted from tags v0.80.0 and v0.83.5 and origin/main 6a45d4b25 (run as the `reflow2 update` wrapper runs it: reflow2_init.py --binary B --update): init --harness vscode-cli with the 0.80.0 kit wrote a receipt listing 72 files, harnesses [vscode-cli]; every new file outside .reflow2/ deleted and tracked files restored; update with the 0.83.5 kit exited 0, created 73 paths (72 kit files + docs/design export; REFLOW2.md in place of AGENTS.md because the test repo had its own AGENTS.md) and edited the same 4 tracked files (+27 lines). Same on main (74-76 paths). why_not_an_update, place_kit_file and installed_manifest are byte-identical in 0.83.5 and main, so the field version and main behave alike.

DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENTS: (1) receipt deleted -> refused, exit 1, nothing written: the receipt is the whole gate. (2) receipt kept but installed_files emptied -> the full kit is still written: the receipt's FILE LIST is not what comes back; the updating kit's own list for the recorded harnesses is. (3) receipt kept, harnesses key removed -> update (no tty) installs for ALL MCP harnesses (.mcp.json, .claude, .vscode, .opencode), a second, worse shape of the same gate. (4) receipt restored from backup unchanged (the reporter's workaround) -> the next update recreates everything again; and each update rewrites the receipt at the new version, so the trap re-arms itself.

REPORT'S CONCLUSION: CONFIRMED that the stores still held a 0.80.0, 72-file receipt and that its presence is why update ran. OVERTURNED in mechanism: update does not "bring the recorded kit forward" from the receipt's list; it performs a full install of the current kit for the recorded harnesses, and a missing file is written because deleting a kit file is the documented way to ACCEPT the kit copy (place_kit_file message; tools/test_init.py:675). There is no recorded state for "this project removed its kit", and no per-project uninstall (SETUP.md offers only `reflow2 install --uninstall`, machine-wide). The receipt lives inside .reflow2/, beside the design, so removing the kit while keeping the design keeps the receipt.

CLASS: the same one fact:defect-a-stale-kit-receipt-silently-decides-whether-the-loop-nudge-is-owed named: a receipt of an install EVENT read as a live fact about the project, here by reflow2_init.py rather than nudge.rs.

NOT ESTABLISHED: the 0.83.5 BINARY was not run (its part, backup/export/merge driver, does not choose which files are written); Anthony's machines were not inspected, so whether his repos still listed the files in .git/info/exclude from the 0.80.0 workaround (dec:idea-init-local-for-a-repository-you-do-not-own) is unknown. No fix chosen.
